pull.title: rest: don't log an error for /spenttxouts on a block without undo data
pull.body:
`/rest/spenttxouts/<hash>` reads the undo file for every block above genesis. For a block that was stored but never connected (a side branch) or whose undo data was pruned, there is no undo position, so `OpenUndoFile()` fails and `ReadBlockUndo()` writes `OpenUndoFile failed for FlatFilePos(nFile=-1, nPos=0)` to debug.log with `LogError`. The request itself already returns 404, but each unauthenticated request for such a block adds an `[error]` line that looks like disk corruption.

This checks `CheckBlockDataAvailability()` for `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` before reading, so nothing is logged. Pruning clears `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`, so pruned blocks are covered too. The response is unchanged.

The new check at the end of `interface_rest.py` requests a stale block and fails on master because of the logged error.

rest: don't log an error for /spenttxouts on a block without undo data

`/rest/spenttxouts/<hash>` calls `ReadBlockUndo()` for every block above
genesis. For a block that was stored but never connected (a side branch)
or whose undo data was pruned, `GetUndoPos()` is null, so
`OpenUndoFile()` fails and `ReadBlockUndo()` writes "OpenUndoFile failed
for FlatFilePos(nFile=-1, nPos=0)" to debug.log with `LogError`. The
endpoint then correctly answers 404, but every unauthenticated request
for such a block adds an `[error]` line that looks like disk corruption.

Check `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` first and only read the undo file when it can
exist. Pruning clears `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`, so this covers pruned blocks
too. The response is unchanged.

The new interface_rest.py check requests a side-branch block and fails
on master because of the logged error.

comments.body: I think the `&& !chainman->m_blockman.IsBlockPruned(*pblockindex)` check here is redundant?
Can this use `CheckBlockDataAvailability` to avoid duplicating the impl?

Thanks, both right. `PruneOneBlockFile()` clears `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`, so the `IsBlockPruned()` check added nothing. It now uses `CheckBlockDataAvailability(*pblockindex, *pblockindex, BlockStatus{BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO})`, in e8af2c7488925e35ffeaf64e523cef48b70280eb.

heh, that's funny. I was talking about `src/rpc/blockchain.h:void CheckBlockDataAvailability(node::BlockManager& blockman, const CBlockIndex& blockindex, bool check_for_undo) EXCLUSIVE_LOCKS_REQUIRED(::cs_main);`, but I guess this works as well.

edit: I was thinking about `CheckBlockDataAvailability` from the rpc, to have more accurate error messages, but maybe that is not too important for the rest interface.
I think a simple `pblockindex->nStatus & BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` is more straightforward tbh but either way works.
yeah, i was thinking that the rpc `CheckBlockDataAvailability` would provide better error messages, but if they are not used, a plain `nStatus & BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` seems fine.
@kriss39 Can you address the nit? I think both reviewers would be happy to re-ack a `nStatus & BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`
Done, switched to a plain `nStatus & BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` in eebc145847b4f05da61e95fcae1b420a6ce3ea0f.
